speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and whether there was any specific injury or bite that preceded it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to fully bend or straighten the finger? Do you notice any bruising or deformity compared to the other fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any numbness or tingling in the fingertip, and is the skin over the joint intact or broken? I need to rule out infection or nerve damage before proceeding.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the mechanism of injury and your inability to flex the distal joint while the finger remains extended, I suspect an avulsion fracture or tendon rupture. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray rules out a fracture, the injury is likely a tendon avulsion. Can you confirm if you are unable to actively flex the very tip of the finger, while still being able to bend the middle joint?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the mechanism of injury, the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, and the negative X-ray, I am confident in the diagnosis of a mallet finger. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
